summary: The note covers the Australian sharemarket's expected strong start on 6 December 2023 despite a slight Wall Street slip, with the Australian dollar dropping. It reports stock moves such as Perpetual's gain and Evolution Mining's fall, and analyst commentary that National Accounts data point to an RBA pause. It also covers US market moves, Treasury yields, Fed rate expectations, crypto gains, and Take-Two's Grand Theft Auto VI news.
one_line: Australian shares got a lift from data pointing to an RBA pause while Wall Street edged lower amid mixed US jobs and services data.
key_facts: Perpetual climbed 6.3 per cent after announcing a strategic review of its three-pronged corporate structure that might see it demerge its corporate trust and wealth management businesses.
Endeavour shares lifted 2.4 per cent after forecasting its hotels division EBIT would grow by more than $150 million over the next five years.
Evolution Mining sank 13 per cent after raising $525 million selling new shares to institutional investors at $3.80 a share.
Moomoo market strategist Jessica Amir said the local market outperformed global equities because National Accounts figures pointed to the Reserve Bank potentially pausing rate hikes.
On Wall Street the S&P 500 edged down 0.1 per cent for its first back-to-back loss since October; the Dow Jones slipped 0.2 per cent and the Nasdaq composite rose 0.3 per cent.
US employers advertised just 8.7 million jobs on the last day of October, down 617,000 from a month earlier.
The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.18 per cent from 4.26 per cent late Monday; it had been above 5 per cent in October, its highest in more than a decade.
The two-year Treasury yield fell from 4.61 per cent to 4.57 per cent after the economic reports.
Traders widely expect the Federal Reserve to hold rates steady at its meeting next week and potentially cut in March, according to CME Group data.
The federal funds rate is above 5.25 per cent, up from nearly zero early last year.

Bitcoin rose above $US43,000 ($65,600) on excitement about a possible exchange-traded fund; Robinhood Markets reported a roughly 75 per cent jump in crypto trading volumes in November and its stock rose 10.3 per cent.
Take-Two Interactive slipped 0.5 per cent after a trailer said Grand Theft Auto VI is coming in 2025, later than some analysts expected.
IAG chief executive Nick Hawkins said the behaviour of Peter Horton, group general counsel and company secretary, didn't meet expectations in its code of ethics and conduct.
